findings.description: In src/config_manager.c, cfg_entry_ok accepts any nonempty, terminated name. SWC-SUP-001 and CON-SUP-115 require an unknown task to be rejected as configuration fault 9; for example, a table entry named "BOGUS" passes this check.
findings.requested_change: Validate each configured task against an authoritative set of known task identities and notify fault 9 for unknown tasks.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_init replaces invalid retained content with an empty state and writes it back. SWC-SUP-026 requires entries that still pass individual checks to remain readable for diagnosis after a non-power-on reset.
findings.requested_change: Preserve and expose individually valid retained entries while recording the loss and latching the safe state; refine the storage interface as needed.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_init records s_last_ms during start-up, but fm_set_operational does not reset it. The first fm_cycle_update therefore includes start-up time in the operational accumulator, contrary to SWR-LAT-006 and SWC-SUP-008; this can clear detection counts prematurely.
findings.requested_change: Start the accumulation interval at the transition to OPERATIONAL and account only for elapsed time in that state.

findings.description: In src/time_service.c, ts_ms returns a millisecond value rounded down at each reading. Subtracting two such readings in fm_cycle_update can over-count an individual interval by up to nearly 1 ms, contrary to SWR-LAT-006's prohibition on over-counting and its 100 us per-update limit.
findings.requested_change: Provide elapsed-time accounting with sufficient resolution and a conservative conversion that cannot over-count operational time.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_notify releases its critical section after recording a detection, then calls oc_safe_state before ws_inhibit. A timer interrupt can detect a fault while the control-cycle task is between fsup_cycle_end and ws_cycle_service; after the detector resumes or is preempted before inhibition, a watchdog service can follow detection, contrary to SWR-WDG-001.
findings.requested_change: Make detection and watchdog inhibition ordered atomically against watchdog service, and specify the resulting concurrency behavior.

findings.description: In src/scheduler.c, sch_tick checks sch_blocked and then separately calls hal_task_release. A timer interrupt can detect a fault between those operations, after which the task is still released, contrary to SWC-SUP-005's prohibition on releases after detection.
findings.requested_change: Serialize the final fault-state check and task release against interrupt-context fault detection.

findings.description: In src/flow_supervisor.c, fsup_checkpoint discards a checkpoint when the four-entry log is full. If the four expected checkpoints have already arrived in order, a fifth duplicate is discarded and fsup_cycle_end reports no fault, although the received sequence differs from the configured order under SWC-SUP-007.
findings.requested_change: Retain an overflow or extra-checkpoint indication and include it in the cycle-end fault decision.

findings.description: In src/diag_comm.c, dc_request_done sets the number of GET FAULTS answer lines to the snapshot length, and dc_render_answer emits END only for an empty snapshot. CON-SUP-134 requires END after the last fault line as well.
findings.requested_change: Append an END line after every nonempty fault-history response and specify that behavior in SWU-DIA-001.

findings.description: In src/diag_comm.c, dc_submit_fault and dc_submit_rst only enqueue records; they do not make the diagnostic task ready. SWC-SUP-039 and DEC-SWC-015 require immediate readiness on report submission to support the first-character deadline.
findings.requested_change: Provide and invoke the architecture's diagnostic-task wakeup mechanism on accepted submissions, with its interface and timing specified.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_retry_pending reads a pending cell, leaves the critical section to submit it, then unconditionally clears the cell. An interrupt can store a newer BUSY report in the same cell during that interval; the later clear loses it, contrary to SWC-SUP-039's no-loss rule.
findings.requested_change: Make pending-cell transfer and release safe against concurrent updates, preserving every report or providing the required bounded admission behavior.

findings.description: In src/cycle_task.c, cyc_part_b ignores HI_E_HW from ws_cycle_service. In src/wdg_service.c that error is returned when hal_wwdg_enable fails, but no fault is notified and the independent watchdog is still serviced. This contradicts SWU-CYC-001's claim that ignored failures have already been notified and can leave operation without the required window watchdog.
findings.requested_change: Define and implement a safe reaction to window-watchdog enable failure, including propagation or fault notification and watchdog-service behavior.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_wait_reports services the independent watchdog on every iteration even when transmission makes no progress. SWC-SUP-002 requires service to stop on stalled transmission so that the watchdog resets; a fixed 100000-iteration limit does not establish that behavior or a time bound.
findings.requested_change: Detect lack of report progress and stop watchdog servicing as specified, with a bounded, verifiable progress criterion.

findings.description: In src/cycle_task.c, cyc_timer_handler calls tsup_on_compare for each due event; each detected event calls fm_notify, which repeats output writes, retained-state writes and report submission. SWC-SUP-062 and DEC-SWC-017 allocate the full safe-state reaction only to the first detection in a coincident pass and rely on a 5 us budget for each later decision.
findings.requested_change: Implement and specify the architecture's bounded handling of subsequent coincident detections, or establish a revised architecture and timing allocation.

findings.description: SWU-TST-001 states that fault_inject.c is excluded from the production build and that this was verified by inspecting the build, but no production build definition is present in the project. The build gate's evidence includes src/fault_inject.c, so the claimed exclusion is not established.
findings.requested_change: Provide a reviewable production build configuration that excludes the test hook and a separate test configuration that includes it; correct the design's verification claim.

findings.description: In src/cycle_task.c, cyc_timer_handler consumes later limit events without calling tsup_on_compare after the first fault or when already SAFE or LATCHED. SWC-SUP-006 and DEC-SWC-017 require each due limit event to be decided, including its detection count and pending report; only the safe-state reaction is to be omitted after the first detection.
findings.requested_change: Decide every due limit event and preserve its required detection and reporting while avoiding repeated safe-state reactions.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_cycle_update accumulates differences between ts_ms readings. As OP-SWU-007 records, these differences can over-count an update by up to 1 ms, contrary to SWR-LAT-006's prohibition on over-counting and its 100 µs per-update under-count limit.
findings.requested_change: Use an elapsed-time accounting method that meets SWR-LAT-006, including retained sub-millisecond remainder and the transition into OPERATIONAL.

findings.description: SWU-TIM-001 specifies that ts_elapsed_u in src/time_service.c never over-counts real elapsed time. Subtracting two quantized timer readings can over-count: readings immediately before and after a counter increment differ by 10 µs even when less real time has elapsed. The specified guarantee therefore does not follow from the implementation.
findings.requested_change: Specify and implement an elapsed-time method whose quantization error satisfies the no-over-count and per-update limits of SWR-LAT-006, including its initialization and remainder handling.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_wait_reports stops after 100000 iterations even if the report remains incomplete and the watchdog has not reset. SWC-SUP-002 requires the report-completion barrier to continue until completion, failure notification or watchdog reset; returning HI_E_STATE delegates subsequent behavior to unspecified caller code.
findings.requested_change: Define and implement a bounded barrier and subsequent behavior that preserve the architecture's completion-or-reset requirement when the iteration limit is reached.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_notify calls ws_inhibit and oc_safe_state for every path A detection. SWC-SUP-006 and DEC-SWC-017 require the safe-state reaction only on the first detection in a coincident-event pass; their 5 us allocation for subsequent decisions depends on that omission.
findings.requested_change: Specify and implement the first-reaction-only behavior while retaining each detection count and report, and reconcile the handler timing allocation.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_cycle_update accumulates ts_elapsed_u results, each reduced by one 10 us unit. At a 10 ms update interval this loses 60 ms over 60 s, exceeding the 10 ms per-reset under-count limit in SWR-LAT-006 and SWC-SUP-008. The SWU-FLT-001 specification incorrectly claims less than 10 us accumulated lag.
findings.requested_change: Revise the elapsed-time accounting and its specification to meet both the per-update and per-reset under-count bounds without over-counting.

findings.description: SWU-TIM-001 describes ts_elapsed_u as under-counting by less than 10 us per call, but its function specification and src/time_service.c subtract one unit and allow an error approaching 20 us. Its description also says nothing is lost between updates, although the subtraction is repeated each call.
findings.requested_change: Make the unit description and function contract consistent with the implemented quantization and the cumulative accuracy required by SWR-LAT-006.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_submit overwrites an existing BUSY pending cell when another report from the same source arrives. The earlier detection then has no report, contrary to SWC-SUP-006 and DEC-SWC-017, which require each coincident detection to be counted and reported.
findings.requested_change: Provide bounded pending-report handling that preserves every report required for the supported detection workload, and specify its capacity and overflow behavior.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_run proceeds to the configuration CRC after su_check_region detects an application CRC fault. SWC-SUP-002 states that a code 1 to 7 fault detected during the checks stops the sequence.
findings.requested_change: Stop the start-up check sequence after the first such fault and update SWU-STU-001 to specify the resulting path.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_run still notifies code 8 when su_submit_rst fails. A code 8 line can therefore be submitted without the preceding RST message required by SWC-SUP-002 and SWU-STU-001.
findings.requested_change: Handle failed RST submission before notifying code 8 so that the required message order is preserved, and specify the failure path.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_run returns when su_submit_rst fails without notifying code 8 for a watchdog reset. SWC-SUP-002 requires a code 8 report after each watchdog reset, including when handling an earlier fault was interrupted.
findings.requested_change: Define and implement a bounded failure path that preserves the required code 8 notification and RST-before-code-8 ordering.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_wait_reports requests a reset after 100000 iterations even if transmission is progressing. SWC-SUP-002 permits the barrier to end on report completion, report failure or a watchdog reset after transmission stops progressing; no elapsed-time or progress bound shows that the iteration limit cannot interrupt a healthy transmission.
findings.requested_change: Bound the barrier using a demonstrated time and progress criterion that allows healthy transmissions to complete and conforms to SWC-SUP-002.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_submit discards a report when its 36-entry pending queue is full. SWC-SUP-008 requires each detection to be submitted for reporting within 10 ms, but SWU-FLT-001 neither bounds all possible arrivals and queue drain time nor guarantees submission before the deadline.
findings.requested_change: Provide and justify bounded admission and transmission behavior that preserves every required report and its submission deadline under the architecture's permitted fault arrivals.

findings.description: In src/time_service.c, ts_init sets the millisecond count to zero only after earlier start-up work and records the current counter as its origin. Consequently ts_ms excludes time between reset and that initialization, although SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003 require milliseconds since the latest reset.
findings.requested_change: Define and implement a reset-referenced time origin, including the interval before time-service initialization, consistent with the timer HAL and the required timestamp.

findings.description: SWU-TIM-001 specifies ts_arm for every 32-bit instant, but ts_diff in src/time_service.c interprets the modular difference as a signed 32-bit distance. Instants at least 2^31 units away are indistinguishable from past instants, so the stated past-event and ordering behavior cannot hold for the specified range.
findings.requested_change: Specify and enforce an unambiguous maximum scheduling horizon and overdue interval, or use a representation that supports the stated full instant range.

findings.description: su_run returns when su_submit_rst fails without notifying code 8 for a watchdog reset. SWC-SUP-002 requires a code 8 report after each watchdog reset, including one that interrupted handling of an earlier fault.
findings.requested_change: Preserve the required code 8 reporting path when RST submission cannot complete.

findings.description: su_wait_reports requests a reset after 100000 iterations even if transmission is progressing. SWC-SUP-002 permits the barrier to end on report completion, report failure, or a watchdog reset after transmission stops progressing; no elapsed-time or progress bound shows that the iteration limit cannot interrupt a healthy transmission.
findings.requested_change: Implement and substantiate a bounded barrier that preserves the architecture's completion, failure and stalled-transmission behavior.

findings.description: fm_submit discards a report when its 36-entry pending queue is full. SWC-SUP-008 requires each detection to be submitted for reporting within 10 ms, but the design neither bounds all possible arrivals and queue drain time nor guarantees submission before the deadline.
findings.requested_change: Provide a defensible arrival and service bound and implement report handling that meets the required deadline for every permitted detection.

findings.description: ts_init sets the millisecond count to zero after earlier start-up work and records the current counter as its origin. ts_ms therefore excludes time between reset and initialization, contrary to SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003.
findings.requested_change: Establish a time origin at the latest reset and account for the elapsed time before initialization.

findings.description: SWU-TIM-001 specifies ts_arm for every 32-bit instant, but ts_diff interprets the modular difference as a signed 32-bit distance. Instants at least 2^31 units away are indistinguishable from past instants, so the specified ordering cannot hold across the stated range.
findings.requested_change: Specify and enforce an unambiguous scheduling horizon, consistent with every caller and the architecture, or use a representation that supports the stated range.

findings.description: SWC-SUP-001 and SWC-SUP-050 require a linker-placed default table with four task identities, periods, order and limits. The design and listed source files validate and access an externally supplied table but do not define those defaults.
findings.requested_change: Provide and trace the required default configuration data in the protected configuration block, including its placement and CRC integration.

findings.description: After a non-power-on reset with an invalid retained part, fm_init salvages valid history entries, appends a loss record and writes the resulting state. If all eight history entries are valid, fm_hist_append replaces the oldest valid entry. SWC-SUP-026 requires entries that pass their individual checks to remain readable without being overwritten.
findings.requested_change: Retain all individually valid entries while recording the storage loss, and specify the storage and reporting behavior for a full history.

findings.description: SWC-SUP-061 identifies OP-SWC-011: T_DIAG may still be within its 20 ms execution limit at the 5 ms flow check. The design checks it at that cycle end, so an otherwise timely execution can be reported as a missing checkpoint; the upstream choice remains unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SWC-011 with the responsible product authority and align the flow and timing design with the selected behavior.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_wait_reports can request a reset after 100000 consecutive unchanged millisecond readings. No execution-time bound establishes that this count cannot be reached within one healthy timer tick. SWC-SUP-002 permits the barrier to end on report completion, failure notification, or watchdog reset after transmission stops progressing.
findings.requested_change: Establish a valid progress-based termination rule and its timing bounds, or obtain an upstream decision that permits the implemented reset behavior.

findings.description: In src/startup_manager.c, su_run returns immediately when fm_is_latched() is true after only one dc_service_step(). On a watchdog reset with an already-set latch, the queued RST and code 8 lines can remain incomplete, although SWC-SUP-002 and SWR-RST-003 require the watchdog-reset report.
findings.requested_change: Keep the latched start-up path servicing the required messages through completion or an explicitly permitted failure or reset outcome, without releasing application tasks.

findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_submit discards a report when the 36-entry pending queue is full. SWC-SUP-008 requires each detection to be submitted for reporting within 10 ms, but the design does not establish that arrivals and drain time prevent overflow or late submission.
findings.requested_change: Provide an implementable admission and transmission strategy with justified arrival and timing bounds that meets the reporting requirements; resolve OP-SWC-013 where a product decision is necessary.

findings.description: SWC-SUP-061 and OP-SWC-011 leave the T_DIAG flow rule unresolved: the design checks at the 5 ms cycle-end phase, although T_DIAG may be within its 20 ms execution limit. A timely execution can therefore be reported as a missing checkpoint.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision and align the flow and timing design with it.

findings.description: SWU-TIM-001 now counts from timer value zero, but OP-SWU-014 records that the inputs do not establish that the target timer runs from reset or that hal_timer_start preserves it. The design therefore does not establish the reset-relative timestamp required by SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003.
findings.requested_change: Establish a supported reset-relative time source and its initialization contract, or resolve the missing platform fact before relying on it.

The design does not establish the reset-relative timestamp required by SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003.

findings.description: src/fault_manager.c fm_submit discards a report when the 36-entry pending queue is full. The design does not establish that arrivals and drain time prevent loss or late submission under SWC-SUP-008.
findings.requested_change: Provide a bounded arrival and service argument that establishes report capacity and deadlines, or revise the reporting design so detections are not discarded.

findings.description: SWC-SUP-061 and OP-SWC-011 leave the T_DIAG flow rule unresolved. The design checks at the 5 ms cycle-end phase although T_DIAG may execute within its 20 ms limit, so a timely execution can be reported as a missing checkpoint.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision and align the flow check and timing design with it.

findings.description: src/time_service.c initializes its accumulated timestamp from timer value zero. OP-SWU-014 records that the inputs do not establish that the timer runs from reset or that hal_timer_start preserves it, so the reset-relative origin required by SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003 is unestablished.
findings.requested_change: Establish a supported reset-relative time source and its initialization contract, then align the unit and port.

findings.description: OP-SWU-011 records that the core clock, CRC throughput and execution times are unavailable. The design cannot substantiate the SWC-SUP-061 execution allocations, the 0.5 ms CRC segment limit or the supervisor processor-time budget.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the missing platform and execution-time evidence and establish the task and processor-time budgets.

findings.description: src/cycle_task.c reports a refused window-watchdog enable as fault code 9 with entity WWDG. CON-SUP-119 specifies CONFIG as the entity for code 9, so this path produces a report inconsistent with the product decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the watchdog-enable failure classification against the requirements and make the reported code and entity consistent with the accepted decision.
